title: Tuning the release profile
subtitle: Change the knobs and watch the trade-offs move
disclaimer: Illustrative trends relative to the default release profile (1.0×), not measurements: real numbers depend heavily on your code and target. Shorter bars are better.

opt.label: opt-level
opt.help: opt-level selects the LLVM optimization pipeline. 3 is the release default, s/z optimize for size (and often lose some speed), 0 is what debug builds use.

lto.label: lto
lto.help: Link-time optimization lets LLVM inline and remove code across crate boundaries. thin is a cheaper, parallel variant; fat merges everything into one module: smallest and fastest, slowest to build.

cgu.label: codegen-units
cgu.help: The crate is split into units compiled in parallel. 16 builds faster; 1 gives the optimizer the whole crate at once, for slightly better code.

panic.label: panic
panic.help: abort removes the unwinding tables and landing pads: smaller binaries and slightly less code in hot paths, but destructors no longer run on panic and catch_unwind stops working.

strip.label: strip
strip.help: Strips symbol names from the final binary. Big size win, no runtime effect, but stack traces and profilers lose function names unless you keep separate debug info.
